cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Tell Me Why
cards.instruction: Get someone to reveal the motive behind a choice by offering small pieces of your own truth as bait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've turned left with you again. Clever shortcut. I take the long way round my old office; why this route?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My former boss catches this train.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Less crowded, naturally. I told mine I'd become a novelist. What did you tell yours?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That I had a better offer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've carried the same blank notebook past mine for a year. Are you avoiding him because there wasn't a better offer?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies turns as shortcut but B2 does not establish it is not one; A3/A5 personal career deception strongly bait motive.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 this-train lacks established station/train and direction of avoidance; A3 then infers evasion. B4 better offer clearly causes A5 matching lie.

relationship.evidence: B2 former boss concern plausible but route relation underexpressed.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 offer to test bluff with own blank notebook.

specificity.evidence: A1 walking/route and B2 this train need one explicit location link.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 notebook specific; A3 less crowded cover does not resolve geography.
